html:
A Fula emirate founded in 1809 by the scholar Modibo Adama, who received a flag from Usman dan Fodio to spread his jihad into the uplands south of Lake Chad.

Adama and his successors set up lamidates, local Fula states, at Yola, Ngaoundere, Garoua, Maroua and elsewhere, owing loyalty to the Sokoto Caliphate. They raided the peoples of the hills for slaves. The Germans and British split the emirate in 1901, with Yola going to Nigeria and most of the land to German Kamerun. The lamidos still hold power in northern Cameroon, and the north's Fula Muslim elite produced Ahmadou Ahidjo. See also the Fula jihads.
